The bag for the Saturday market

Last Saturday, Mum and I ____1____ (walk) to the small market near our home. We took a cloth bag instead of carrying several new ones. I had drawn a green apple on its side the evening before.

The market had many ____2____ (stall). Some sold food, and others sold plants or handmade things. We stopped ____3____ a table covered with little cakes. Mum asked about the ingredients before choosing one for each of us.

I carried ____4____ (I) cake in a paper box. The seller closed it ____5____ (careful) so that the soft top would not touch the lid. She reminded me to keep the box upright while we walked.

Mum wanted ____6____ (buy) tomatoes next. We looked ____7____ some that were ready to eat that day, rather than the hardest ones on the table. The seller let us choose the number we needed.

The cloth bag became ____8____ (heavy) than it had been when we left home. Before ____9____ (put) the cakes inside, we placed them above the tomatoes where they would not be crushed. The picture of the apple was almost hidden by the folded handles.

At home, we unpacked everything together and washed the tomatoes for lunch. The bag could be folded and used again. Mum said its bright picture made it easy to recognise. I decided to add ____10____ orange on the other side another day. For now, the cake was waiting, and it had arrived with its soft top still in place.

The umbrella with a loose handle

During a rainy week, our classroom had a row of wet umbrellas beside the door. On Thursday, I ____1____ (notice) that the handle of mine was loose. I did not try to fix it while walking through the crowded entrance.

Several ____2____ (friend) waited with me until the corridor was clear. We put the umbrella ____3____ a tray so it would not leave water across the floor. The teacher helped me contact Dad before the journey home.

Dad checked ____4____ (I) umbrella that evening. The problem was with one small fastening, not with the fabric. He looked ____5____ (careful) at how the parts fitted together before deciding what could be done.

I offered ____6____ (help), but he explained which work he would do himself and where I could stand safely. I held a light ____7____ him while he checked the handle. We tested it indoors without opening it near anyone's face.

The repaired handle felt ____8____ (firm) than before. After ____9____ (finish), Dad wrote down which part had needed attention. If it loosened again, he would know what to inspect rather than guessing from the beginning.

The next morning, I carried the umbrella in its cover. I still checked it before going out. A repair was not a promise that nothing could ever go wrong, but it had dealt with the specific problem. I was glad we had not thrown away ____10____ otherwise useful object. Its yellow fabric had been easy to recognise in the classroom row, and now I could use it again without worrying about the handle slipping free.
